findings.claim: The check that decides whether the script runs as the entry point builds its URL with `new URL(`file://${invokedPath}`)`. That breaks when the path contains '#', '?' or '%', and also when the path goes through a symlink (import.meta.url is the real path, but argv[1] is not). In those cases main() never runs, and `pnpm verify:rounds-index` exits 0 without comparing anything. The gate fails open. `tools/docs/state-index/check.mjs:1182` already uses `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href`.
findings.fix: Import `pathToFileURL` (or use `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === realpathSync(process.argv[1])`) and use the same idiom as check.mjs so the gate cannot pass silently.

findings.claim: The suite covers idempotence, filename/id mismatch and cycles. It has no negative case for `--check` against a stale or missing index, which is exactly what `verify:rounds-index` protects in `pnpm check`. It also has no renderer cases for cross-round links, two terminals, a missing predecessor or unreadable JSON. The acceptance section of CTG-SEAL only asks for these on the combined suite, and they are covered only on the state-index side.
findings.fix: Add tests where `--check` exits non-zero after changing one byte of the index or deleting it, and add the missing supersession negatives on the renderer side.

D-2 also adds a generic rule ("só emite o PC após merge, CI verde e PASS da outra família"). That goes a little beyond item 3 of SEAL-AUTHORIZATION, which only asked to tie D-1/D-2 to R-0017.

findings.claim: `work/rounds/*/record.md` is taken out of format:check, but no continuous gate covers it. Only the one-time `round seal` validates it. A later hand edit of any record.md would go unnoticed. The index does have `verify:rounds-index`, so its exclusion is justified.
findings.fix: Record this as known, or have `verify:state-index` / a sensor check that each record.md's `phase_closure` matches the round's terminal PC.
